angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 738,833 km at 176.72 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.6588 +/- 0.0175 mas (same row, RUWE 1.09): 176.72 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.062 +/- 0.027 solar radii from Yee et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-4463 A b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJS..265....1Y/abstract): 738,833 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.056 +/- 0.059 solar masses from Yee et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-4463 A b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJS..265....1Y/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5640 +/- 89 K from Yee et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4463 A b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJS..265....1Y/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Yee et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4463 A b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJS..265....1Y/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-4463-a.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.409, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
